Subject: POC sizing inputs & SLAs (VentureX)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the team was impressed. We're ready to scope a 6-week POC and need a quick sizing and cost-backed recommendation to share with our infra team. High-level workload:~
- Peak concurrent users (chat sessions): ~45 concurrent writers during peak (US East)
- Average request: ~350 tokens generated, 20 tokens input prompt on average
- Request profile: 80% text-completion/chat, 20% embeddings/rerank
- Target p95 latency SLO for text generation: <= 450 ms
- Expected average qps (sustained): 12 qps, burst to 40 qps for short windows
- Model preference: open-model family (Llama 2 13B / Mistral / similar) but open to recommendations

Can you provide: tokens/sec estimates per GPU for candidate model variants, p95 latency fit vs SLO, recommended reserved GPU count for predictable throughput plus suggested buffer/headroom, and an outline of trade-offs (quantization, batching, context length). I've attached a small sample of request logs.

Thanks,

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: POC sizing inputs & SLAs (VentureX)

Karthik / team — did the math and wrote up assumptions below. Long story short: recommend starting the POC on a small H100 pool for latency-critical paths and allow A100-backed spare capacity for cost-effective throughput for batchy workloads. Numbers are conservative (no kernel-level boosts).

Assumptions
- Average output tokens per request: 350 tokens
- Avg internal token size/time distribution: 50% decode time, 50% KV/cache overhead at 4k context window
- Effective tokens/sec observed in benchmarks (per GPU, single-stream throughput, mixed load):
  - Llama2-13B fp16 on A100-80GB: ~1,600 tokens/sec
  - Llama2-13B fp16 on H100-80GB: ~2,300 tokens/sec
  - Llama2-13B int8 (LLM.int8) on A100: ~2,400 tokens/sec (with accuracy regression risk ~1–3%)
  - Mistral-like 13B fp16 on H100: ~2,700 tokens/sec
  - Mistral-like 13B int4 quant on H100: ~3,600 tokens/sec (experimental, watch regressions)

Latency model (p95 end-to-end generation)
- Single request of 350 tokens without batching: tokens/sec inverted + overhead -> expected p95
  - A100 fp16 (1,600 tps): 350/1600 = 219ms compute + 120ms misc = ~339ms p95
  - H100 fp16 (2,300 tps): 350/2300 = 152ms + 120ms misc = ~272ms p95
  - H100 int4 (3,600 tps): 350/3600 = 97ms + 120ms misc = ~217ms p95

Effect of batching
- Small batching (batch sizes 2–6) increases overall throughput but adds tail latency for single-stream requests. For p95 <= 450ms we must cap batching for latency-critical endpoints (max batch ~4 for H100).

Capacity sizing (sustained 12 qps; burst 40 qps)
- Convert to tokens/sec requirement:
  - Sustained: 12 qps * 350 tokens = 4,200 tokens/sec
  - Burst: 40 qps * 350 tokens = 14,000 tokens/sec

- GPUs required (rounded up) by configuration (target p95 <= 450ms, recommend 25% headroom):
  - H100 fp16 (2,300 tps):
    - Sustained base: ceil(4200/2300) = 2 GPUs -> add 25% headroom => 3 GPUs
    - Burst runway: ceil(14000/2300) = 7 GPUs -> add 25% headroom => 9 GPUs
  - H100 int4 (3,600 tps, experimental):
    - Sustained: ceil(4200/3600) = 2 -> add headroom => 3 GPUs
    - Burst: ceil(14000/3600) = 4 -> add headroom => 5 GPUs
  - A100 fp16 (1,600 tps):
    - Sustained: ceil(4200/1600) = 3 -> add headroom => 4 GPUs
    - Burst: ceil(14000/1600) = 9 -> add headroom => 11 GPUs
  - A100 int8 (2,400 tps):
    - Sustained: ceil(4200/2400) = 2 -> add headroom => 3 GPUs
    - Burst: ceil(14000/2400) = 6 -> add headroom => 8 GPUs

Operational recommendations
- Recommended runway for the POC: provision 5 H100s (3 for sustained + 2 spare for burst), with autoscaling to add up to 9 if we see bursts > 30 qps. This balances latency SLO and predictability for a 6-week POC.
- If VentureX prioritizes cost and accepts a small latency delta, A100 + int8 profile at ~3–4 reserved A100s for sustained plus autoscale to 11 for burst is more economical but increases complexity and tail risk.
- Quantization notes: int8/int4 gives big tps boosts but requires validation with your prompt set; recommend a quality gate in the POC (small eval set) before enabling for production traffic.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts could reduce effective tokens/sec by up to 15–30% in practice—factor this into headroom planning.

Next steps / deliverables (for Monday):
- I'll produce a 1-page table with exact GPU counts, cost ballpark (monthly), and p95 estimates per mix (H100/A100, fp16/int8/int4).
- Rohan: can you validate autoscale policy constraints (cold-start time, pre-warm) for H100 fleets?

--

Liam / Sophia — appreciate the quick turnaround from Marcus. TL;DR recommendation and next actions below.

Recommended POC config (6 weeks)- Reserve: 5 x H100-80GB (primary pool)
- Autoscale cap: 9 x H100 for burst headroom (fast scale-up path)
- Fallback: 3 x A100-80GB warm pool for cost-effective batch jobs and reranking
- Quality gate: run int8/int4 experiments in parallel on a shadow pool; do not enable for live inference until QA eval passes (explicit acceptance criteria)

Why this mix- 5 H100s provide the sustained headroom to keep p95 well under 450ms for 12 qps while allowing short bursts without SLA breaches.
- Having a small A100 warm pool reduces cost for rerank/embedding requests and gives operational redundancy.

Mutual action plan
1) Redwood delivers a 1-page sizing & cost summary + short runbook (by EOD today) — Marcus + Rohan
2) VentureX signs the PO for a 6-week reserved POC capacity (recommended 5 H100s) — Target sign by 5/14
3) Redwood sets up the pools, pre-warms KV caches with the sample workload, and runs an initial smoke test (3–4 hours) — Target 5/18
4) Joint QA + int8 experiments in week 2 of the POC; decision point at week 3 on production roll-forward

Ask from your side
- Please confirm acceptance of the 5 H100 recommendation or indicate if you'd prefer an A100-led initial config (I can produce a quick cost delta).
- Confirm your procurement lead and timing so Marissa can attach the PO terms.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call today to walk through the table.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
